title: Jerk Chicken
subtitle: Jamaican jerk-marinated grilled chicken
excerpt: Jerk chicken is Jamaica's most iconic dish: deeply spiced, smoky, and fiercely aromatic. Chicken pieces are coated in a punchy marinade of scotch bonnet, allspice, and thyme, then grilled until charred at the edges and cooked through. It is bold, crowd-pleasing food that works equally well for a weekend barbecue or a midweek dinner.
sourceNotes: Jerk seasoning originates with the Maroon communities of Jamaica, who developed the technique of slow-cooking meat over pimento wood as a method of preservation and flavour development. The spice blend has been refined over centuries and is now one of the most recognised flavour profiles in the Caribbean.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the chicken overnight in the refrigerator for the best flavour. Eight hours is the minimum; up to 24 hours is even better.
recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze cooked jerk chicken in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the marinade and chicken for a crowd. Cook in batches on the grill.

content.text: The key to great jerk chicken is time: the longer the marinade sits, the deeper the flavour penetrates the meat. Score the chicken pieces before marinating so the spice paste can get into the flesh. If you do not have a grill or barbecue, a very hot griddle pan or oven grill works well.
Score the chicken legs with a sharp knife, making 3 to 4 deep cuts through to the bone on each piece. This allows the marinade to penetrate properly and helps the chicken cook evenly.

Blend the chillies, spring onions, garlic, ginger, allspice, cinnamon, thyme, soy sauce, lime juice, sunflower oil, and brown sugar in a food processor or blender until a rough paste forms. Taste and adjust the chilli level if needed.

Put the chicken in a large dish or zip-lock bag and pour over the jerk marinade. Work the paste into the cuts and all over the surface. Cover and refrigerate for at least 8 hours, or ideally overnight.
Remove the chicken from the refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking to take the chill off. Preheat your grill, barbecue, or griddle pan to medium-high heat.

Cook the chicken over medium-high heat for 35 to 40 minutes, turning every 10 minutes. You want a good char on the outside while the interior cooks through. If the outside is colouring too quickly, move the pieces to a cooler part of the grill or reduce the heat.

Check the chicken is cooked through by piercing the thickest part near the bone: the juices should run clear. If you have a meat thermometer, the internal temperature should reach 75°C. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve with rice and peas and a squeeze of fresh lime. Any leftovers can be shredded and used in wraps or salads the next day.

items.symptom: The outside is charred but the chicken is still raw inside
items.cause: The heat is too high, or the chicken pieces are very thick and went straight from the fridge to the grill.
items.fix: Move the chicken to a cooler zone and continue cooking with indirect heat. Allow the chicken to come to room temperature before cooking. For very thick pieces, finish in a 180°C oven for 10 to 15 minutes after searing.

items.symptom: The marinade tastes flat and the chicken lacks punch
items.cause: Insufficient marinating time, or the marinade was not worked into the scored cuts.
items.fix: Always marinate for at least 8 hours. Make sure to score the meat deeply and press the paste into each cut. Add a little more allspice and lime juice to the paste next time.

items.symptom: The chicken is sticking to the grill
items.cause: The grill grates were not oiled, or the chicken was moved too soon before the surface had a chance to caramelise.
items.fix: Oil the grill grates before cooking. Leave the chicken undisturbed for at least 8 to 10 minutes before attempting to turn it; it will release naturally once a crust has formed.
